title: Dedicated capacity - Autoscale cost/SLA synchronization & Q2 spike plan
creator: Asha Patel
description: Run a focused Q2 spike to align pricing/cost models, autoscale knobs, and SLA obligations for Dedicated capacity. Goal: produce a validated decision matrix that prescribes autoscale policies per pool type (reserved, hedged, burst) and the corresponding pricing guardrails and SLOs for GA. Deliverables: runbook, policy matrix, telemetry dashboard queries, and a pilot launch plan.
acceptance_criteria: Decision matrix completed and reviewed by Eng, Infra Finance, and Sales Ops
Pilot autoscale policy implemented in a staging Dedicated pool with metrics captured for 7 continuous days
Cost vs latency impact analysis completed with a recommended default policy for small/medium/large pools
SLA wording drafted for Dedicated offering reflecting autoscale fallback behavior and customer-visible limits
Roadmap entry and release checklist added to console-2026.04 release plan
tasks: Run historical workload sweep and segment pools by burstiness (ENG data task)
Prototype predictive warm-pool signal (ENG-4210 spike / telemetry)
Model unit-cost delta for batching vs single-request paths (Finance+Research)
Write canary plan for policy rollouts and abort conditions
Draft customer communication + SLA appendix for autoscale fallback behavior
Create dashboard queries and alerts for pilot (Console/Observability)
decisions: Use three default autoscale profiles: conservative (SLA-first), balanced (cost-latency trade), aggressive (cost-first for non-critical pools)
Pilot will surface both on-demand warm and hedged reserved capacity as independent signals — not merged in first run
Fallback ordering: same-region reserved -> hedged reserved -> cross-region burst -> model-variant fallback
Chargeback model during pilot: attribute incremental GPU-hours to pool owner; present a forecasted monthly delta in pilot dashboard
